messages:
maya (CS): Quick async — LumenEdge renewal account saw repeated webhook 5xxs overnight. I opened a support ticket but wanted to loop eng early since renewal call is next Wed and they're worried about reliability. TL;DR: our delivery to their endpoint is getting 502/timeout around the inference.complete events. Sample log below. @sam can you take a quick look at retry/backoff behavior?

sam (eng): Thanks — can you paste a representative request id + the raw response body/headers? Is it always the same webhook path or varied routes?

maya (CS): Good Q. Happened for routes: /v1/events/inference.complete (all customers), but only LumenEdge saw the spike. One request id: req_20260317_8a9f. Log: ```POST /v1/events/inference.complete 2026-03-17T03:12:02Z req=req_20260317_8a9f -> status=502, resp_body="Bad Gateway", upstream_timeout=true, retries=2```

kevin (support): Ticket LUM-342 created with LumenEdge. They attached a stack trace from their side showing nginx 502 + a note that payloads > 120KB sometimes cause upstream to drop. Link: https://support.redwood.dev/tickets/LUM-342 (internal)

sam (eng): Hmm payload size could be it. Our router proxies have a 128KB default buffer in the config. If payloads spike we might see upstream_connection_reset from client side. Can you share the actual payload size for that req id? Also tagging @deploy-bot to check if there were noisy restarts on infra around 03:10-03:20 UTC.

maya (CS): Payload for that req was 145KB. Customer said they send base64 audio in the metadata sometimes. Renewal meeting scheduled 2026-03-24. Customer is nervous but still leaning renewal — wants visible remediation plan.

deploy-bot: infra: no restarts detected on routing pool-12 between 03:00 and 04:00 UTC. CPU and mem within normal; p95 latency for webhook workers spiked from 120ms -> 980ms.

sam (eng): Ok that matches buffer + downstream timeout. Two options: 1) change our router limit to accept larger payloads (ops/config change) + increase timeouts, 2) suggest LumenEdge switch to payload-hosting link (pre-signed URL) and send pointer. Option 1 is quicker for short-term but has capacity implications. Which path do we prefer for renewal risk?

alina (AE): For the renewal convo we need a short-term patch + longer-term ask. If engineering can push a fast config bump and a note to the customer about sending hosted payloads as next step, that'll likely be enough. Customer asked for ETA and rollback plan.

sam (eng): I can prototype a config change in a canary for routing pool-12: increase buffer to 256KB and bump timeout to 10s. Will also add telemetry to count >120KB deliveries. Timeline: canary today EOD PT, monitor for 2h, then roll to wider pool tomorrow morning if stable. Rollback will be immediate to previous config if error rate rises.

maya (CS): That sounds good. I'll tell the customer: we plan a canary today, full rollout tomorrow if stable, and also propose they migrate to payload links for long-term. Will also ask them to reduce base64 embedding if possible.

kevin (support): I'll attach the canary plan & telemetry checks to ticket LUM-342, and update severity to P1 for visibility.

sam (eng): One ask for CS: when you send quote for the canary/rollout, include example request ids for the time window so we can correlate. Also any customer-side logs (nginx) will help.

maya (CS): Will do, sending the ids now. Thanks all. Will post a short summary for the renewal call once canary completes. :thumbsup:
